claims.text: The baseline catalyst is an equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
Colloidal or chemical reduction can produce the baseline catalyst with uniform particle size and composition.
The controlled intervention is a 5–10% relative increase in Rh content while holding nanoparticle size, dispersion, and processing conditions constant.
Increasing the Rh fraction shifts the d-band center of surface active sites.
Increasing the Rh fraction may enrich Rh at the catalyst surface.
The Rh-induced electronic-structure change alters the adsorption configuration of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The d-band-center shift optimizes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates.
Modified surface electronic interactions adjust catalyst bond strengths with ethanol and its intermediates.
The adjusted adsorbate bond strengths lower the activation barrier for ethanol-oxidation steps.
Lower oxidation barriers enhance ethanol-oxidation activity.
Relative to the equimolar baseline, the Rh-enriched catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Relative to the equimolar baseline, the Rh-enriched catalyst will have a higher ethanol-oxidation current density.
The proposed mechanism should hold in acidic aqueous ethanol at moderate temperatures up to approximately 80–100 °C under fuel-cell-like potential cycling.
Extensive sintering or phase segregation under prolonged high-stress operation may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Reaction-induced changes in surface composition or particle morphology could offset the initial activity benefits of Rh enrichment.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes cases involving sintering or phase segregation, but the falsification rule treats rapid degradation as falsifying the Rh/d-band activity hypothesis without requiring confirmation that the catalyst remained within those structural boundaries.
